findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: The skim milk and whole milk in the standing cooler by the coffee bar were observed to not be date-marked. The PIC stated that they typically go through whole milk quickly. If the whole milk is used within 24 hours, there does not need to be date-marking. The PIC stated that they go through skim milk less often and the skim milk had a use by date of 9/29/2026. The skim milk was voluntarily discarded during the inspection due to being past the use by date. Ensure that the skim milk is being date-marked if it is not opened and used within 24 hours. TCS foods that are opened or prepared in-house and are held for over 24 hours should be date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer buckets in Ginna’s Cafe and the sanitizer bucket in Fuzzi Wigs were all observed to only be at 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium. findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
There are clear, packaged containers of bagels, muffins, and other food items in the facility that do not have any labels on them. All items that are packaged for the consumer need to have labels on them. This label must include the common name of the food, a list of ingredients and sub ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight (if made of two or more ingredients), including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD, all major allergens, an accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents, and the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor. This was discussed with the PIC. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling.

During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(B) In food that is not time/temperature control for safety food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, such as bins of sugar, flour, or cinnamon.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The facility is observed to be using a plastic cup as a scoop for the sugar in the sugar container in the dry storage area. A cup is not a sufficient scoop, as it is not durable, easily cleanable, and does not have a handle. Ensure that the plastic cup is replaced with a proper scoop with a handle. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: There was little to no date marking observed within the facility. All TCS food, including all milks, cut vegetables, cheese, etc, that is prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours should be clearly marked to indicate day 1, being the date of being opened or prepared, and discarded at the end of the 7th day. A follow up will be conducted on 9/6/2024 to ensure that date marking is being done. 

 (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: There are single service spoons that are facing various directions. Ensure that the spoons are all facing the same direction to avoid contamination to the food contact surface of the utensil. There are also single service food boats that are not inverted and have the food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that all single service articles and utensils are inverted to protect them against contamination. 

 (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips

Ensure that Quaternary ammonium test strips are obtained for both places to allow proper testing of the sanitizer. A follow up will be conducted on 9/6/2024 to ensure that test strips are now in both places. 

A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed holding pot of chili to be measured at 115F. Observed holding pot of chicken dumpling soup to be measure at 114F. Per PIC, soup was placed in hot holding approximately 2 hours prior to inspection. Soups were placed on stove and reheated to 165F. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed prep cooler at Ginna’s Cafe to not be holding TCS foods at proper cold holding temperatures. 2 containers of roast beef were measured at 52F. 1 container of ham was measured at 51.6F. 1 container of chicken was measured at 54F. One container of mozzarella cheese was measured at 59F. One container of cut tomatoes was measured at 56F. 2 containers of cut greens were measured at 58F. All TCS food that were measured at over 41F were discarded. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13  (Pf) An irreversible registering temperature indicator is not provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature in the mechanical warewashing machine. Employee is not able to verify if the hot water is properly sanitizing. Provide appropriate hot water temperature-sensitive tape or paper thermometers. Reference 4-302.13.  Facility manager obtained a new max registering thermometer from another department in the facility.  Corrected on site

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11  (C) Observe personal employee food in fudge cooler next to butter. Areas designated for employees to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that food, equipment, linens, and single-service and single-use articles are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Observed the preparation cooler to be holding foods in the low 50s (cottage cheese probed-50F, chicken salad probed - 54F, and pickles probed for temp check - 54F). Service conducted on cooler within past week - likely hole in hose/compressor. Service call was made. Icing product for duration of service day; discard at end of day.  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41F.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).
